references.text: God's promise to Abraham that those who bless him will be blessed, and those who curse him will be cursed, reflects the blessing given to Jacob.
The Lord's word to Rebekah that the older shall serve the younger, which is fulfilled in Isaac's blessing of Jacob.
Isaac tells Esau that he has made Jacob his master and given all his brothers as servants to him—a direct fulfillment of the blessing in verse 29.
Balaam's blessing of Israel uses almost identical wording: 'Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you.'
A messianic psalm speaking that all kings shall bow down before him and all nations serve him, similar to the blessing Jacob receives.
Edom (Esau's descendants) became David's servants, a historical fulfillment of the prophecy that Jacob would rule over his brother.
Paul refers to God's sovereign choice of Jacob over Esau, citing both Genesis 25:23 and Malachi 1:2–3 as confirmation of the blessing.
Isaiah's prophecy expands upon and fulfills the patriarchal promise that nations will bow before God's chosen one.
Jacob's blessing over Judah repeats and further develops the promise of his brothers' submission from Genesis 27.
Balaam's confirmation that God's blessing is irrevocable supports the principle in Isaac's blessing.
